digest.headline: The Nasdaq entered a correction as the DAX reached a record close and the yen neared 160 per dollar.

lede.b: The Nasdaq stock market index fell by more than 10% from its recent peak, which is called a correction when a group of company shares drops significantly in price. This means the total value of those technology companies decreased rapidly. At the same time, strong inflation data came out, which shows that the cost of living and everyday prices are rising. This strong inflation data made the US dollar currency stronger against other currencies. The Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States and acts like the main bank that sets interest rates for the whole country, faced higher expectations from markets that it will raise borrowing costs.
lede.i: The Nasdaq entered a correction after dropping over 10% from its recent peak. Strong inflation figures simultaneously bolstered the US dollar and drove up expectations for Federal Reserve interest rate hikes. Markets adjusted their pricing for central bank borrowing costs as these macroeconomic data points landed.
lede.a: The Nasdaq breached correction territory following a 10% drawdown from recent peaks. Concurrently, robust inflation prints triggered a repricing of Federal Reserve terminal rate expectations, strengthening the dollar. Market participants adjusted duration and equity risk premium assumptions across technology holdings.

items.b: The Nasdaq entered a correction after dropping over 10%, while Nvidia shares fell 8% in after-hours trading.
items.i: The Nasdaq entered a correction following a 10% drop, while Nvidia shares declined 8% in after-hours trading.
items.a: The Nasdaq entered a correction after a 10% drawdown, compounded by an 8% after-hours slide in Nvidia shares.

items.b: The DAX 40 index hit a record close of 26,662.77 points as Siemens Energy shares surged by 9%.
items.i: The DAX 40 index reached a record close of 26,662.77 points driven by a 9% surge in Siemens Energy shares.
items.a: The DAX 40 index printed a record close at 26,662.77 points, propelled by a 9% rally in Siemens Energy.

items.b: The Japanese currency traded near 160 per US dollar while top currency diplomat Mimura issued new warnings.
items.i: The Japanese yen traded near 160 per dollar, prompting top currency diplomat Mimura to issue intervention warnings.
items.a: The yen hovered near 160 per dollar as top currency diplomat Mimura reiterated intervention risks amid ongoing carry trade dynamics.

items.b: Petrobras revised its 2026 capex guidance upward and the Ibovespa index gained 0.42% to 172,060 points.
items.i: Petrobras raised its 2026 capex guidance following strong third-quarter results, and the Ibovespa rose 0.42% to 172,060 points.
items.a: Petrobras upwardly revised 2026 capex guidance on robust cash generation, lifting the Ibovespa 0.42% to 172,060 points.

thread.b: Global markets reacted to shifting technology stock values and currency movements. Central bank expectations changed as economic data came out in different countries. Commodity prices and oil outputs also shifted across various regions.
thread.i: Global equity markets absorbed technology sector corrections and semiconductor headwinds. Currency valuations shifted as central bank policy expectations adjusted to incoming price data. Commodity producers navigated changing production targets and demand pressures.
thread.a: Cross-asset volatility persisted as technology equity drawdowns coincided with shifting central bank rate trajectories. Currency markets tested key psychological thresholds under pressure from rate differentials and intervention threats. Commodity supply dynamics adjusted through OPEC output shifts and corporate capex revisions.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US markets face inflation pressure and tech sector shifts

stories.t: Nasdaq Enters Correction Amid Tech Stock Movements
stories.b: The Nasdaq is an index, which is a basket of major technology shares. Shares are tiny slices of ownership in a company. The Nasdaq has slid into a correction. This means it dropped by 10% or more from its recent high. Nvidia shares sank 8% after hours following a report that its board may oust Huang. Meanwhile, CoreWeave surged 25%.
stories.i: The Nasdaq entered a correction after dropping over 10% from recent peaks. Nvidia shares fell 8% in after-hours trading on reports that the board might oust Huang. CoreWeave shares surged 25%, offsetting some tech losses. Cerebras Systems secured a $1 billion OpenAI deal.
stories.a: The Nasdaq slid into a correction as idiosyncratic governance risks hit mega-cap bellwethers. Nvidia shares dropped 8% post-market on reports concerning CEO Huang, triggering broader futures downside. CoreWeave surged 25% to cushion the broader index blow, while Cerebras Systems locked in a $1 billion OpenAI agreement.

stories.t: Inflation Data Strengthens Dollar and Fed Hike Expectations
stories.src: The New York Times · Financial Times · marketscreener.com
stories.b: Inflation is the rising cost of everyday items over time. Strong US inflation data boosted the US dollar. Gold prices slipped as a result. Investors also increased their expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike. The Federal Reserve is the central bank of the United States, which sets monetary policy.
stories.i: Strong US inflation figures bolstered the dollar and pushed gold prices down. Markets raised Federal Reserve interest rate hike expectations following the data release. The broader US economy continues to defy turbulence.
stories.a: Hot US inflation prints catalyzed dollar strength and drove spot gold lower. Rates markets aggressively repriced Federal Reserve tightening paths, lifting hike probabilities. Macro resilience persists despite political turbulence.

politics.b: Surging US economic activity defies worries over turbulent Trump politics.
politics.i: The surging US economy defies worries over turbulent Trump politics.
politics.a: Resilient macroeconomic prints defy systemic concerns over a turbulent Trump administration.

timeline: CoreWeave surges 25% while Nvidia rebounds in a US stock rally.
Gold slips as strong inflation data bolsters the US dollar and Fed hike expectations.
Nasdaq futures fall as Nvidia sinks 8% after hours on a report that its board may oust Huang.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Deutsche Bank sees further UK price growth upside

stories.t: Deutsche Bank Projects Higher Price Pressures
stories.b: Deutsche Bank expects inflation, which measures how fast everyday prices rise, to go up further. This means people will likely pay more for goods and services in the future. The bank shared this view in a recent market update.
stories.i: Deutsche Bank projects additional upside for UK inflation. The institution released this assessment through its market analysis channels. Traders monitor these revisions to gauge future central bank policy moves.
stories.a: Deutsche Bank models further upward momentum in UK inflation prints. This projection alters the expected path of the policy rate terminal point. Rates markets must reprice real yields based on this incoming trajectory.

politics.b: There is no political news today.

timeline: Deutsche Bank publishes a report seeing further upside for United Kingdom inflation.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: German DAX reaches record close as stocks surge

stories.t: DAX 40 Reaches Record Close
stories.b: The DAX 40 is an index, which is a group of major company shares tracked together to show how the market is doing. This index hit a record close of 26,662.77 points. Siemens Energy saw its shares soar by 9%. European shares logged record closes driven by artificial intelligence optimism.
stories.i: The DAX 40 index hit a record close of 26,662.77 points. Siemens Energy shares surged by 9%. European shares logged record closes fueled by artificial intelligence optimism involving CoreWeave and Siemens.
stories.a: The DAX 40 printed a record close of 26,662.77 points. Siemens Energy shares rallied 9% amid broader inflation and technology tailwinds. European equities logged record closes driven by artificial intelligence optimism tied to CoreWeave.

stories.t: German Trade and Economy Updates
stories.b: The German trade surplus narrowed despite rising exports. German inflation eased. The German economy recovered faster than expected with growth accelerating towards year-end.
stories.i: The German trade surplus narrowed despite rising exports. German inflation eased according to market reports. The German economy recovered faster than expected with growth accelerating toward year-end.
stories.a: The German trade surplus narrowed despite rising exports. German inflation printed softer readings. The German macroeconomic recovery outpaced consensus expectations with growth accelerating toward year-end.

politics.b: No political updates were provided in the sources.
politics.i: No political updates were provided in the sources.
politics.a: No political updates were provided in the sources.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Japanese currency warnings and equity movements

stories.t: Japanese Yen approaches 160 threshold against the dollar
stories.src: The Lufkin Daily News · FXStreet · Bloomberg.com
stories.b: The Japanese yen is the money used in Japan. It is getting very weak compared to the US dollar. One dollar now buys nearly 160 yen. Government officials in Japan are warning that they might step in to stop this drop. The currency recently fell to a two-month low before recovering slightly.
stories.i: The Japanese currency trades near 160 per US dollar, prompting fresh warnings from officials. Top currency diplomat Mimura tells markets not to forget previous intervention risks. The carry trade dynamics and rate hike bets from the central bank influence these moves. The currency recently rebounded slightly from a two-month low.
stories.a: Spot rates approach the 160 per US dollar threshold, triggering verbal intervention from currency diplomat Mimura. Market participants weigh potential official buying against existing positioning and monetary policy expectations. The currency recovers modestly from a two-month low as rate hike speculation contends with intervention threats.

stories.t: Nikkei edges higher as technology shares advance
stories.b: Japan's main stock index is called the Nikkei. It went up slightly today. Companies related to technology did well. However, suppliers connected to Nvidia saw their share prices drop.
stories.i: The Nikkei index edges higher in recent trading sessions. Technology sector strength supports the broader market gains. Nvidia-linked suppliers act as a drag on the index.
stories.a: The Nikkei index registers modest gains driven by pockets of technology sector strength. Index performance remains constrained by downward pressure on Nvidia-linked supply chain equities. Trading reflects localized sector divergence rather than broad directional momentum.

politics.b: Japanese financial leaders are speaking out about the value of their money. Officials like Mimura are warning traders about rapid currency drops. The Bank of Japan is also holding meetings and giving speeches about monetary policy.
politics.i: Japanese currency officials issue repeated warnings against speculative inflation-linked currency pressures. Diplomat Mimura highlights ongoing risks of official intervention. Central bank board members deliver regional speeches detailing price and policy stances.
politics.a: Fiscal and monetary authorities maintain verbal pressure against unilateral currency depreciation. Currency diplomat Mimura reiterates intervention warnings as spot levels approach critical psychological barriers. Board member Asada outlines regional economic activity and price dynamics in Nagasaki.

timeline: Bank of Japan releases account statistics
Currency diplomat Mimura warns markets as yen nears 160 per dollar

China.label: China
China.sub: Yuan bond demand, corporate buybacks, and fuel prices

stories.t: Chinese Yuan Debt Draws Inflows
stories.b: Global investors are buying more Chinese yuan bonds. Bonds are loans that governments or companies issue to raise money, paying regular interest until they are paid back. This demand comes as the world sees a boom in Chinese yuan debt. More people want to hold these assets. Investors are putting their money into these Chinese financial products.
stories.i: Global investors are increasing their exposure to Chinese yuan bonds. The market is experiencing a broad boom in domestic debt issuance. Portfolio managers are reallocating capital toward yuan-denominated fixed income assets. Foreign demand for these instruments continues to climb.
stories.a: Non-resident capital inflows into Chinese yuan bonds are accelerating amid a broader market boom. Cross-border portfolio managers are reweighting fixed-income allocations toward mainland debt instruments. Yield differentials and currency considerations drive the sustained accumulation of these yuan-denominated assets.

stories.t: CMOC Funds Buyback via Bank Loan
stories.b: CMOC secured money for a share buyback. A share buyback is when a company buys its own shares back from the market to reduce the total number. China Merchants Bank gave the company a special loan of up to 1.8 billion yuan. This loan gives CMOC the funding it needs for the buyback. The bank announced this dedicated financial support.
stories.i: CMOC secured funding support for a share buyback through a dedicated credit facility. China Merchants Bank pledged up to 1.8 billion yuan in a specialized loan for the transaction. This credit line provides the exact capital required for the corporate repurchase plan.
stories.a: CMOC secured dedicated liquidity for its equity repurchase program via a credit facility. China Merchants Bank extended a targeted loan of up to 1.8 billion yuan to backstop the transaction. The earmarked capital structure provides the precise leverage needed to execute the corporate buyback without tapping operational cash reserves.

stories.t: China Retail Fuel Prices Face Reduction
stories.b: China's pump prices are dropping for the sixth time this year. Global crude oil prices are falling. Drivers will save about 15 yuan when filling up a standard tank. The government adjusts these prices based on global markets. Crude oil is the raw material used to make petrol.
stories.i: Chinese pump prices are set for their sixth reduction of 2026. Global crude slumps are driving the downward revision in domestic fuel costs. Motorists will save approximately 15 yuan when filling a standard tank. The pricing mechanism reflects international benchmark declines.
stories.a: Domestic retail fuel pricing adjustments are tracking international crude benchmarks lower. The impending reduction marks the sixth downward adjustment for Chinese pump prices in 2026. The localized cost savings translate to roughly 15 yuan per full tank based on prevailing refined product formulas.

politics.b: China completed a major tax transition for offshore trusts, with declared taxes reaching over 160 billion yuan. Meanwhile, Russia stopped trying to replace the US dollar with the Chinese yuan after years of promoting currency alternatives.
politics.i: China concluded its offshore trust tax transition, registering declared taxes exceeding 160 billion yuan. Concurrently, Russia abandoned its prior efforts to promote currency alternatives and replace the US dollar with the Chinese yuan among BRICS partners.
politics.a: Tax authorities finalized the offshore trust tax transition, capturing declared obligations in excess of 160 billion yuan. Simultaneously, Russia stepped back from its multi-year initiative to supplant the US dollar with the Chinese yuan within the BRICS framework.

timeline: Russia steps back from its effort to replace the US dollar with the Chinese yuan.
China Merchants Bank pledges up to 1.8 billion yuan in a dedicated loan for CMOC.
China declares taxes topping 160 billion yuan after wrapping up an offshore trust tax transition.

India.label: India
India.sub: Rupee rises while indices point upward

stories.t: Indian Rupee Reaches Seven-Month Peak Against Dollar
stories.b: The Indian rupee is the official money used in India. It just reached a value close to a high not seen since April, hitting 93.69 against the US dollar. Money coming into the country from foreign investors helped push this value up. A strong US dollar tried to pull the value back down, but the foreign money won out.
stories.i: The Indian rupee touched a level near its April peak, trading at 93.69 per dollar. Foreign financial inflows provided upward momentum to the currency. This appreciation happened despite resistance from ongoing dollar strength.
stories.a: The Indian rupee consolidated near its April high at 93.69 against the greenback. Cross-border capital inflows countered broader greenback strength to drive the currency to a seven-month peak. The exchange rate action reflects sustained overseas allocations offsetting external currency pressures.

stories.t: Stock Futures Rise Following Regional Gains
stories.b: Stock futures known as GIFT Nifty moved upward. This pointed to a steady and positive start for major indices like the Sensex and the Nifty 50. Asian stock markets also moved higher. Meanwhile, Nvidia shares dropped by 7% to 8% after regular trading hours, and crude oil prices declined.
stories.i: GIFT Nifty futures advanced to indicate a positive opening for the Sensex and the Nifty 50. Broader Asian equities posted gains during the session. Global technology sentiment faced pressure as Nvidia shares dropped 7% to 8% in after-hours trading, while crude oil prices moved lower.
stories.a: GIFT Nifty futures pointed to a steady open for domestic benchmarks, aligning with broader advances across Asian markets. Equity sentiment absorbed an after-hours drop of 7% to 8% in Nvidia shares. Concurrently, crude oil prices edged downward.

politics.b: No political updates are reported for today.
politics.i: No political updates are reported for today.
politics.a: No political updates are reported for today.

timeline: Nifty futures show a positive intraday outlook
Indian rupee climbs to a near seven-month high against the dollar

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras updates its outlook and the Ibovespa rises

stories.t: Petrobras lifts targets for production and spending
stories.b: Petrobras is a massive oil company controlled by the Brazilian state. It just told the public it will spend more money on its projects in 2026. This is money used to buy equipment and build things, which businesses call capital expenditure. The firm also raised its goals for how much oil it plans to pull from the ground. Record cash generation and high output numbers in the third quarter drove these higher targets.
stories.i: Petrobras revised its 2026 capex guidance upward following strong third-quarter results. Record production and robust cash generation underpinned the expansion in operational targets. Management also outlined plans to extract an additional 500,000 barrels per day from existing platforms.
stories.a: Petrobras adjusted its 2026 capital expenditure guidance alongside Q3 earnings, reflecting improved free cash flow dynamics. The firm targets 500,000 barrels per day of debottlenecking capacity across legacy platforms, signaling an aggressive push for asset sweating. This upward revision in both output ceilings and capital allocation implies management has higher conviction in realized margins and operational uptime.

stories.t: Ibovespa finishes trading day higher
stories.b: The Ibovespa is the main stock market index for Brazil, which tracks the performance of the country's biggest publicly traded companies. This index closed up 0.42%. It finished the session at 172,060 points. This gives a snapshot of how shares across the nation performed on the whole.
stories.i: The Ibovespa index tracked upward during the session. Benchmark equities gained 0.42% to settle at 172,060 points. The move reflects broader market sentiment across domestic equities.
stories.a: The Ibovespa closed 0.42% higher at 172,060 points, capturing broad participation across the domestic equity complex. The advance reflects local price action in the absence of major macroeconomic catalysts. Market participants continue to price domestic risk through the lens of large-cap corporate earnings.

politics.b: The government plans to send the energy minister to Venezuela. This trip happens alongside rising interest from Petrobras in regional energy matters.
politics.i: Brazil will dispatch its energy minister to Venezuela. The diplomatic visit coincides with growing corporate interest from Petrobras in the neighbouring energy sector.
politics.a: Brazil scheduled a ministerial delegation to Venezuela involving the energy minister. The diplomatic mission aligns with corporate maneuvering by Petrobras regarding regional hydrocarbon opportunities.

timeline: Petrobras releases third-quarter earnings and raises 2026 capex guidance
Reports emerge that Brazil will send its energy minister to Venezuela

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Saudi oil output rebounds toward prewar levels as prices drop

stories.t: Saudi Arabia Oil Production Rebounds Toward Prewar Levels
stories.b: OPEC is a group of countries that work together to control how much oil they pump. This group saw its overall oil production jump by nearly 2 million barrels per day in October. Saudi Arabia led this surge as its national production bounced back. Total output now sits close to where it was before the war in Iran started. This happened even though maritime attacks took place.
stories.i: OPEC crude production rose by nearly 2 million barrels per day in October. Saudi Arabian production rebounded sharply during the month. Total output across the group recovered toward prewar levels seen before the conflict in Iran. This supply expansion occurred despite ongoing maritime attacks.
stories.a: OPEC output expanded by nearly 2 million barrels per day in October, driven by a Saudi Arabian production rebound. Aggregate output recovered close to prewar levels established prior to the Iran conflict. Production scaled higher despite maritime security disruptions.

stories.t: Saudi Aramco Cuts Official Selling Prices for Crude Oil
stories.b: Saudi Aramco is the state oil company of Saudi Arabia. The company lowered its official selling prices for buyers in Asia and Europe. Market competition forced the pricing adjustment downward. The changes affect how much refineries in those regions pay for crude.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco reduced its official sale prices for clients in Asia and Europe. Intense market competition drove the downward revision in pricing. The state-owned exporter adjusted these pricing formulas to protect its market share.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco lowered official selling prices for Asian and European destinations. Competitive market pressures forced the pricing concession. The adjustments reflect shifting supply dynamics as group production normalises.

politics.b: Saudi Arabia managed oil output changes while dealing with regional security risks. State energy policy adapted to shifts in global supply and market competition.
politics.i: Saudi officials navigated production adjustments while managing regional maritime security risks. State-directed output scaled toward prewar volumes despite ongoing geopolitical friction.
politics.a: Saudi policymaking balanced output normalisation against maritime security vulnerabilities. State production targets tracked broader OPEC trajectory adjustments amidst competitive regional pricing pressures.

timeline: Saudi Aramco reduces official oil sale prices for Asia and Europe
OPEC reports crude production rose by nearly 2 million bpd in October

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Nigeria records crude output and foreign exchange movements

stories.t: Nigeria maintains oil production targets
stories.src: The Sun Nigeria · Punch Newspapers · CNBC Africa
stories.b: Crude oil production reached 1.69 million barrels per day in October. This output meets the target set by OPEC, which is a group of oil-producing countries that manage supply, for the sixth month in a row. OPEC says the near-term outlook for the country is improving.
stories.i: Crude output averaged 1.69 million barrels per day in October. This marks the sixth consecutive month that production met the OPEC quota. The oil cartel views the near-term outlook for the country as improving.
stories.a: October crude production printed at 1.69 million barrels per day, sustaining compliance with the OPEC quota for a sixth straight month. OPEC reiterated an improving near-term outlook for Nigerian output volumes. Monitoring trajectory hinges on sustained security in producing regions to prevent supply shocks.

stories.t: Foreign reserves and currency value shift
stories.b: Foreign exchange reserves dropped below $55 billion. At the same time, the naira depreciated against the United States dollar. Market reports noted significant exchange rate movements on November 11, 2026.
stories.i: Foreign exchange reserves fell below $55bn. Concurrently, the naira depreciated against the US dollar, marking notable downward movement in the exchange rate. These currency pressures coincided with reserve depletion.
stories.a: FX reserves contracted below the $55bn threshold. The naira registered sharp depreciation against the US dollar amid diminished reserve buffers. The implied trajectory depends on central bank intervention capacity and capital flow dynamics.

politics.b: The federal government paid 143 billion naira in arrears to health workers. President Tinubu announced a reward of 100 million naira for each player in the Flamingos team after their under-17 World Cup victory. President Tinubu also asked the House of Representatives to approve a loan plan worth 10.79 trillion naira. In regional budgets, the Kano State government planned to spend over 1 trillion naira in 2027.
politics.i: The federal government disbursed 143 billion naira to settle health workers' arrears. President Tinubu promised 100 million naira to each member of the Flamingos squad following their under-17 World Cup win. Separately, the executive submitted a request to the House of Representatives for a 10.79 trillion naira borrowing plan. Kano State announced fiscal plans aiming to spend over 1 trillion naira in 2027.
politics.a: Disbursements totaling 143 billion naira cleared outstanding health worker arrears. Executive commitments extended to 100 million naira awards per player for the Flamingos under-17 World Cup squad. Legislative engagement proceeded as President Tinubu requested House approval for a 10.79 trillion naira borrowing program. Sub-nationally, Kano State outlined a 2027 budget targeting expenditures exceeding 1 trillion naira.

timeline: Kano State targets over 1 trillion naira in its 2027 budget proposal.
Federal government clears 143 billion naira in health workers' arrears.
President Tinubu offers 100 million naira to each Flamingos player for the under-17 World Cup win.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: ASX slips on mining losses while tech shares rally

stories.t: Mining Declines Offset Tech Gains on Australian Exchange
stories.b: The main share index in Australia fell slightly. Mining companies dropped in value. Technology companies went up in price. Tech shares kept the overall market stable.
stories.i: The Australian Securities Exchange slipped as mining shares declined. Information technology shares extended their prior rally. Technology gains cushioned the impact of commodity sector losses on the benchmark index.
stories.a: The broader ASX index contracted due to downward pressure on resources. Tech sector outperformance absorbed a portion of the materials drag. Market breadth reflected sector divergence between mining and software equities.

stories.t: Australian Dollar Reaches Ten-Month Lows
stories.b: The Australian currency dropped in value. It fell near its lowest point in 10 months. Foreign exchange markets traded the currency downward.
stories.i: The Australian Dollar declined toward 10-month lows. Currency traders pushed the exchange rate lower. The foreign exchange market reflected sustained selling pressure on the domestic currency.
stories.a: The Australian Dollar depreciated toward the bottom of its 10-month range. Spot pricing tested multi-month technical supports. Cross-border flows drove the currency deeper into its prevailing downward channel.

politics.b: No government policy updates or political announcements were reported in the financial markets today.
politics.i: No macroeconomic policy decisions or government announcements influenced trading sessions today.
politics.a: Fiscal and regulatory policy variables remained absent from active market pricing today.

timeline: ASX slips as mining losses outweigh technology sector gains.
Australian Dollar declines toward 10-month lows on foreign exchange markets.
